title: config_drift_check._fetch_pyproject sends a Bearer token with urllib's default redirect handler
evidence: src/py_ci_shared/config_drift_check.py:60-70: headers carry Authorization Bearer for urls starting https://api.github.com/, then urllib.request.urlopen(Request(...)) with no custom opener (grep for _SameHost|build_opener in that file: no match). Contrast src/py_ci_shared/ci_health.py:326-339 where _SameHostRedirects exists because CPython copies Authorization to the redirect target.
failure_scenario: A contents-API call answered with a 302 to another host (CDN, proxy fault, API change) delivers CONSUMER_READ_TOKEN (read access to every private consumer repo) to that host.
proposed_fix: Reuse ci_health's same-host opener (move _SameHostRedirects to a shared module) in config_drift_check; test with a local redirecting server asserting no Authorization header reaches the second host.

title: lint-blocking tool pins fall back to unpinned uvx/pip when the PIN input is empty
evidence: .github/workflows/lint-blocking.yml:182,195,205,214,225,238,283: 'if [ -n "$PIN" ]; then uvx "zizmor==$PIN" .; else uvx zizmor .; fi' (same shape for actionlint, codespell, yamllint, bandit, vulture, deptry). Defaults exist (lines 96-124) but a caller passing '' gets the newest PyPI release; black-filtered.yml:93-96 documents this exact drift as a past incident.
failure_scenario: A compromised or merely breaking new release of a lint tool runs in every consumer CI with the checkout (and, for deptry, the installed project) in scope; a red from an unreviewed release looks like a real finding.
proposed_fix: Drop the else branches: empty pin falls back to the declared default or fails with ::error::. Meta-test: every uvx / uv pip install in .github/workflows is == pinned on every executed path.

title: install-pyutilz passes the ref to git fetch/checkout without the shape guard the other workflows use
evidence: .github/actions/install-pyutilz/action.yml:41-45: git -C pyutilz fetch --depth 1 origin "${INPUTS_PYUTILZ_REF}" and checkout with no case guard and no '--'. gates.yml:73-75 and lint-advisory.yml:138 have the guard.
failure_scenario: A ref starting with '-' from the caller's pyproject pin is parsed by git as an option (--upload-pack=... runs a command). Needs a hostile pin in the caller's own repo, so low likelihood.
proposed_fix: Add the same case guard, use checkout --detach and '--' separators.

title: pyutilz cloned from the default branch and not verified against a full SHA
evidence: .github/actions/install-pyutilz/action.yml:34 'git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/fingoldo/pyutilz.git' then checkout of the input; nothing asserts HEAD equals a 40-hex pin.
failure_scenario: If the pin is a tag or branch (allowed), the code installed into consumer CI changes without any consumer commit.
proposed_fix: Reject non-40-hex refs, or assert git rev-parse HEAD equals the pin after checkout.

title: Direct ${{ inputs.* }} substitution into run: in docs.yml, mypy-full.yml, lint-blocking.yml
evidence: .github/workflows/docs.yml:47 'run: ${{ inputs.install-command }}', mypy-full.yml:73, lint-blocking.yml:269; zizmor ignore at docs.yml:44 with the reason 'caller-controlled'. gates.yml:90-93 uses env + bash -c instead, so the repo is inconsistent.
failure_scenario: Exploitable only if a consumer wires the input from untrusted context (PR title, head_ref); the reusable workflow offers no protection and the 'trusted' claim is unenforced.
proposed_fix: Switch to env + bash -c "$INSTALL_COMMAND" as gates.yml does (keeps multi-line script semantics), or document that the input must be a literal.

title: github.action_path interpolated inside a run: script
failure_scenario: action_path is runner-controlled, so no practical injection; zizmor may flag it and a path with quotes would break the command.
proposed_fix: Pass via env ACTION_PATH and use "$ACTION_PATH".

title: tarfile.extractall without a filter on Python < 3.12
evidence: src/py_ci_shared/consumer_import_census.py:214-222: filter='data' only when sys.version_info >= (3,12); else branch relies on a manual isfile/isdir plus '..'/absolute check, marked nosec B202. Input is git archive of a local library.
failure_scenario: Mode bits (setuid) are not stripped on 3.9-3.11, the supported floor; practical risk near nil since the archive is the user's own repo, but the guard is hand-rolled.
proposed_fix: Reject members with setuid/setgid bits in the manual check, or extract per member via extractfile on all versions.

title: release trust depends on repository settings the code cannot verify
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:111-113 comment: environment protection and moving RELEASE_TOKEN into the environment are settings the owner sets. Token read at release.yml:138 and :187; rollback job gated to refs/heads/master (line ~169). A fine-grained contents+workflows token force-pushes the v1 tag every consumer fetches.
failure_scenario: If RELEASE_TOKEN is still a repository secret and the environment has no v* tag rule, any workflow in this repo (including one added on a branch) can read it; compromise moves @v1 for all consumers.
proposed_fix: Owner action: confirm the token lives only in the release environment with a v* deployment rule and a required reviewer; add a ci-health style check of gh api repos/.../environments/release that fails when protection is absent.

title: Verified clean record: no pull_request_target, actions SHA-pinned, least-privilege permissions, safe deserialization
evidence: grep pull_request_target in .github: no match; grep for uses: lines with a non-40-hex ref: empty; all 14 workflows declare top-level 'permissions: contents: read'; release.yml uses persist-credentials:false and passes the token as a one-shot extraheader; run_git (src/py_ci_shared/_core/git.py:109-137) strips GIT_DIR location vars via git_env unless inherit_location; yaml.load uses a SafeLoader subclass (ci_install_covers_conftest.py:206); no shell=True/pickle.load/eval/os.system found in src.
failure_scenario: Not a defect; recorded so the next round does not re-audit.
proposed_fix: None. Confirm existing meta-tests cover SHA pins and top-level permissions.
disposition: WON'T FIX: verified-clean record, no defect
